change: One-token decode routing: the strict decode kernel's key bound is replaced by the measured crossover against the WMMA decode shape (_STRICT_DECODE_WINS_UNTIL_KEYS = 4096 in hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/gemma4/gemma4_attention.py).

why.old_rule: tokens <= 1 and keys <= gemma4_decode_max_keys() (15856 at head_dim 512) -> strict decode kernel.
old_rule_was_wrong_twice: Its premise (a WMMA tile wastes 15 of 16 query rows) stopped holding when a one-token block started selecting the 2-row, 8-GQA-head decode shape, so one of two rows is wasted, not fifteen of sixteen.

The strict decode kernel's own grid is tokens * num_heads = 16 blocks, the same low-parallelism limitation the key split exists to work around. Its cost turns super-linear while the WMMA decode shape stays nearly flat.
why.old_rule_also_over_promised: At head_dim 512 the strict path cannot launch above 15616 keys (its shared-memory validation takes the max of the block and decode requirements), but the rule admitted it to 15856. A context in [15617, 15856] was accepted at construction, prefilled successfully, and raised on its first decode: 'NotImplementedError: Gemma 4 gfx1100 attention requires 66276 bytes of shared memory for head_dim=512, keys=15801'.

crossover_measurement.method: One layer, tokens=1, identical buffers and arguments in both arms, alternating repetitions, median of 9.
crossover_measurement.threshold_rationale: The measured crossover, and below both capability bounds, so the rule cannot reach the [15617, 15856] window.

end_to_end.command: env -u HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES PYTHONPATH=. HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1151 .venv/bin/python scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py --artifact <artifact> --prompt P --output 128 --context P+128 --samples 3 --warmup 1 --expect-gpu 8060S
end_to_end.note: Same device, same artifact, same harness. The 'before' column is the recorded ladder and boundary re-run from the same session family; the 'after' column is this unit.
end_to_end.shape_of_the_win: Decode is now flat at ~28 tok/s from 4096 to 8192 keys instead of collapsing to 16.83 in the middle. The pre-change ladder dipped to 16.83 at 8192 and recovered to 25.98 at 32768, which is the strict kernel's super-linear cost dominating the middle of the range.
end_to_end.correctness_window_closed: A 15800-token prompt, which previously raised NotImplementedError on its first decode, now returns normally: 4 tokens generated.

gate.evaluator: docs/EXECUTION-PROFILES.md section 6 KL envelope over full-vocabulary teacher-forced rows

baseline_capture.why_not_reproducible_from_the_tree: The baseline is the strict kernel at this range, which is no longer the default there. It was captured by temporarily setting _STRICT_DECODE_WINS_UNTIL_KEYS to 10**9, then restoring the file. The restore was verified by sha256: 6f13a733a84264dd84903c038ab5690d73dfe27645e66c902639591c630e5286, identical before and after.
baseline_capture.command: env -u HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES PYTHONPATH=. HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1151 HIPENGINE_EXECUTION_PROFILE=production .venv/bin/python scripts/gemma4_teacher_forced_gate.py capture --prompt 8192 --prefill 4096 --context 8320 --out /tmp/gate_strict_8k.npz

verdict.reproducible: kl_max reproduced to all 17 digits across two independent runs (0.12121157196647189), so it is a deterministic row, not run-to-run noise.

breach_analysis.finding: kl_max is 2.4x over its threshold and is the only failing check. kl_mean, kl_p95 and kl_p99 are 20x to 1000x inside theirs. It is one row of 4095: kl_max is ~2000x kl_p99.

margin_report.band_definition: margin is p1 - p2 within the frozen baseline row

breach_analysis.reading: Every one of the 4095 rows is confident: the smallest top-1-over-top-2 margin is 0.905. The breach is therefore a probability-tail difference on a near-one-hot row, not a changed decision, and top-1 is identical on every row. The gate's own margin_report docstring states the case: 'A single kl_max cannot distinguish a probability-tail difference at a near-one-hot row from a changed decision at a near-tie, and the frozen chain is almost entirely the former.'

isolation.question: Is the breach the 2-row decode shape, or the WMMA online-softmax reassociation itself?
isolation.conclusion: The reassociation is fine at this range: the WMMA prefill shape, which shares the online-softmax walk and the slice combine, passes at 0.0229. The breach is specific to the 2-row, 64-slice decode shape.
isolation.shape_and_slices_are_coupled: The two arms differ in two things, not one: shapes [2] vs [16] and slice_counts [64] vs [16]. Both attempted independent pins were rejected by the planner -- '--wmma-full-shape decode --wmma-full-slices 16' and '--wmma-full-shape prefill --wmma-full-slices 64' each produced shapes [] and slice_counts [], and fell back to the default plan, reproducing the unforced kl_max exactly. So the shape cannot be varied without its slice count through this interface, and the breach cannot be attributed to one of the two from these runs.
isolation.not_established: Whether the tail is the 2-row grouping or the 64-way split. Separating them needs a plan the planner will accept, which does not exist today.

gate.already_shipped_at_other_ranges: The same decode shape with the same 64 slices is the default above 15856 keys, where the strict kernel cannot launch at all. Its gate there passed at kl_max 1.22e-3 over 527 rows (benchmarks/results/2026-10-02-gemma4-teacher-forced-gate-wmma-full-decode-shape.json). So the arithmetic this change extends to 4097-15856 is already promoted; what is new is its coverage of this range, where it measures a worse tail.

reasoning: The measured win is large and paired: 1.688x decode at 8192 keys, 1.113x at 4096.
top-1 is identical on all 4095 scored rows (top1_flips 0, top1_rate 1.0), so greedy output is unchanged everywhere in the range.
kl_mean, kl_p95 and kl_p99 are 20x to 1000x inside their thresholds; the single breach is a tail difference on a row whose decision margin is at least 0.905.
The arithmetic is already the shipped default above 15856 keys under its own passing gate.
It closes a real correctness window: contexts in [15617, 15856] previously raised on their first decode.
The alternative at this range is the strict kernel, whose cost turns super-linear precisely here.
decision.revert: One constant: set _STRICT_DECODE_WINS_UNTIL_KEYS back to gemma4_decode_max_keys() to restore the previous routing (at the cost of the 1.688x and of the [15617, 15856] window reopening).
decision.open_question_for_the_lead: Whether a 0.121 tail KL on 1 of 4095 confident rows is acceptable in exchange for 1.688x decode at 8192 keys. The numbers above are the whole case in both directions.

not_supplied_by_this_evaluator: the 500-1000 paired-row promotion standard (this is 4095 single-chain rows)
